stories.title: Genesis unlock with 7 buckets
stories.description: Genesis token supply is defined with a max supply and a total supply. The circulating supply is monitored by the mint authority. The emission schedule defines the inflation, issuance, and release schedule. Vesting schedules are tracked with a 1-year cliff lockup and team, investor, advisor, community, and ecosystem buckets for unlock cadence. Staking incentives objective utility behavioral goals are funded via a yield source (subsidy / transaction fees / revenue) with sybil abuse controls to prevent gaming wash trading. Reflexivity death spiral risk and sell pressure are evaluated. AMM liquidity pool depth, treasury runway reserves, voting multisig admin key governance authority, and timelock emergency guardian quorum risk controls are established. Disclaimer: not financial advice and not legal advice. This depends on assumptions evaluated via sensitivity stress tests, scenario analysis, and downside risk models. A qualified legal review by counsel has validated securities compliance across regulatory owner jurisdictions.

Scenario schema and headless runner
stories.description: A TokenLab simulation operator or future agent can define an existing-class simulation in versioned YAML or JSON, execute it headlessly, and receive a manifest plus lineage-bearing output tables without changing existing simulation behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A strict YAML/JSON scenario covers economy, controllers, agent pools, Monte Carlo settings, seed, and artifact format.
The factory constructs existing TokenLab classes and edits no existing simulation class.
The headless runner emits an atomic manifest and lineage-bearing CSV or Parquet tables.
The reference scenario matches the deterministic hand-written notebook 01 simulation on the fixed seed.
Existing regression, Z1 parity, fresh-clone, annotation, and Program checks pass.
stories.notes: T-INTAKE-277FB9E6; additive existing-class orchestration verified on Python 3.10 with fixed-reference parity, full regression, Z1 golden parity, installed-wheel smoke, atomic artifact review, and no legacy simulation source diff.

stories.title: Generated artifacts stay out of Git tracking
stories.description: As a TokenLab maintainer, I can regenerate simulation and report artifacts without dirtying Git, while development-only Z1 helpers remain in maintained script and test locations.

acceptance_criteria.description: Regenerating TokenLab and Z1 reports does not add generated outputs to Git status.
Reusable Z1 helpers live under scripts/z1_m3 or tests, and all live imports reference their maintained locations.
The supported Python 3.10 regression suite and the clean regeneration checks pass after artifact cleanup.

stories.title: Inspect simulation artifacts in a simple dashboard

acceptance_criteria.description: A user can open a local read-only dashboard and load the versioned public demo artifact bundle without configuring a database or external service.
The dashboard displays only metrics declared by the artifact profile and clearly labels unavailable tokenomics fields instead of inferring them.
The dashboard provides loading, empty, partial-data, invalid-artifact, and successful states on desktop and mobile-sized viewports.
Artifact paths and uploaded content are size-limited, parsed without code execution, and never sent to a remote service.

The public repository description and topics accurately describe TokenLab's current simulation and tokenomics scope.
